title: Ninco Classic / N-Digital

scope.basis: Classic 1:32 track, borders, N-Digital road devices and track-side accessories from manufacturer catalogues 2012 and 2015.
excluded: Raid and Snow surface variants pending dedicated appearance references
10511–10515 extension kits including roundabout, dune and special curves
Older powerbase revisions not shown in the selected scope
Complete circuit sets, cars, controllers, power supplies and loose cables
Other Ninco track systems and smaller-scale toy ranges
scope.availability: Historical catalogue coverage; no claim of current manufacture or stock.

defaults.note: Ninco radii/lengths from 2012. 180/90 mm cross-section from ScaleAuto’s manufacturer comparison, consistent with the 180 mm radius step. Single-lane width and centred offsets inferred. Border width is illustration-only.

sources.title: Ninco manufacturer catalogue 2012, pages 6–7
sources.note: Manufacturer publication hosted by retailer. Visually inspected; contains precise outer radii, road dimensions and N-Digital pictures.

sources.title: Ninco manufacturer catalogue 2015, pages 10–11 and 14–15
sources.note: Manufacturer publication hosted by retailer. Visually inspected for identities, quantities, road markings and accessories.

sources.title: ScaleAuto manufacturer comparison drawing — Ninco width and lane spacing
sources.note: Secondary-to-Ninco dimensional evidence: another manufacturer explicitly labels Ninco as 180 mm wide / 90 mm spacing. Its rounded radii are not substituted for Ninco’s precise catalogue values.

visualStyle.road: Rough black plastic, bright paired rails and broad black connector tabs
visualStyle.markings: Plain standard track; staggered white grid markings; red/white chevron islands on special sections
visualStyle.borders: Full-width red/white stripes following historical catalogue drawings
visualStyle.accessories: Red/white/grey double-rail barriers, mesh and stone walls, red banking and elevation hardware

sourceIssues.detail: Ninco publishes outer radii 241.37–961.37 mm. Comparison charts round to 242–962 mm; this pack retains Ninco’s values.
2012 lists six 100 mm borders; 2015 lists two. Quantity is null until the intended product revision is established.
The 200 mm border is mislabelled 10223 and taper set 10206 in the 2012 layout. The 2015 catalogue resolves them as 10203 and 10216.
50 mm is a drawing assumption, so no border has a fit model. Red/white follows the selected historical catalogue; plain-black revisions are not verified here.
Catalogue photographs identify products, but do not fully dimension slot transitions, sensor positions, housing envelopes or kit inventories. These remain illustrations.
